transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Polaris CTO), Liam O'Connor (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Alvarez (PM)

---
00:00 Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intros?
00:05 Maya Chen: hi I'm maya, CTO at Polaris, we build an analytics platform for energy infra, focusing on alerts and anomaly detection.
00:12 Liam O'Connor: liam here, i own model infra and integrations, curious about latency/cost and how much work to swap over to an openai-compatible endpoint.
00:20 Priya Rao: great, i'm priya, solutions engineer on inference. i'll be leading the benchmark plan and helping with SDKs and the integration bits.
00:30 Jordan Kim: cool. agenda - scoping the poc: success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, timelines, and specifics around SDKs/function calling/structured output. any additions?
00:38 Sofia Alvarez: can we also cover security briefly? SSO and KMS are must-haves.
00:42 Jordan Kim: yep will cover.

02:15 Priya Rao: quick q - are you planning to use Redwood hosted, dedicated, or private?
02:20 Maya Chen: initially hosted to move fast, but we'll evaluate dedicated or private for compliance down the road.
02:25 Liam O'Connor: we have some regs around data residency, so VPC peering or private deployment will likely be required for production. but pilot can be hosted.

04:00 Priya Rao: for the pilot, what's the workload? is it mostly short chat prompts for alerts or longer summarizations?
04:08 Liam O'Connor: mostly short structured prompts - we send sensor telemetry snippets, ask for anomaly classification and structured fields: {anomaly:bool, severity:int, root_cause:enum, confidence:float}. occasional longer summaries for incident reports ~200-400 tokens.
04:30 Priya Rao: ok that helps. for sizing, estimate concurrency? requests per second?
04:35 Maya Chen: peak about 25 req/s, average 6 req/s. bursts up to 60 for incident storms.
04:45 Priya Rao: great. target latency? you mentioned realtime-ish?
04:50 Liam O'Connor: for the short ones p95 under 350ms would be ideal, median much lower, and the longer summaries we can tolerate up to 800-1000ms.
05:05 Priya Rao: noted. for quality success criteria how do you plan to judge correctness?
05:10 Sofia Alvarez: product wants >=90% accuracy on anomaly label and confidence calibration within +-0.1 for top-tier signals. also structured JSON output must conform to our schema with small variance.

07:00 Priya Rao: on integration side, we support OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints and native SDKs (python/js/go). You can basically swap your openai client with minimal changes. We also support function calling / tool-calling patterns and post-processing hooks for structured output.
07:20 Liam O'Connor: how complete is the function calling compatibility? we use openai function calling heavily.
07:25 Priya Rao: quite mature - we emulate the function calling semantics: model returns a function call object, then you call the tool. caveat: model variants and fallback behavior can differ slightly across models; we'll provide a sample shim.
07:40 Jordan Kim: we can share a sample repo with integration patterns: OpenAI-compatible client replacement, streaming, and structured output validation.

09:15 Maya Chen: does the SDK handle automatic retries and batching? we want to avoid writing heavy infra at the start.
09:22 Priya Rao: yes, SDK supports client-side batching and orchestration for small requests, plus automatic retry/backoff. On the server side our runtime does continuous batching and KV cache to reduce cost for repeated prefixes.

11:00 Liam O'Connor: metrics - we want to run a replay of one week of traffic. what's the benchmarking approach?
11:10 Priya Rao: typical: 1) run a lightweight functional validation on a representative prompt set, 2) run a deterministic correctness eval against your labeled examples, 3) run throughput/latency benchmarks with traffic replay at scaled rate (we'll provide a load script), 4) measure cost per 1k tokens and p95/p50 latency. we recommend including quantized model variants to compare cost/latency.
11:35 Jordan Kim: we'll instrument traces and token-level cost breakdown so you can see where cost comes from.

13:00 Liam O'Connor: about models - which ones should we try? we prefer open models; cost is a big driver.
13:10 Priya Rao: for structured short outputs we often start with a 7B-13B variant quantized for throughput; for higher quality summaries try 70B or 13B higher-accuracy variant. Redwood can route to cheaper variants in low-latency paths. We'll include model suggestions in the pilot plan.

15:00 Maya Chen: security: SOC2 is required, SSO via SAML/Okta, and we need KMS integration for customer keys. Also audit logs for model inputs/outputs.
15:10 Jordan Kim: Redwood supports SOC2 compliance, SAML/Okta SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted we offer customer-managed keys via our KMS bring-your-own-key option; for private deployment you have full control. We will share the security pack.

17:30 Sofia Alvarez: timeline - how long to get pilot live?
17:35 Priya Rao: typical pilot setup 3-7 business days if using hosted with sample prompts. Dedicated/private takes longer due to infra and security reviews, usually 2-6 weeks. For this pilot I'd estimate 2 weeks end-to-end including benchmarking.
17:50 Jordan Kim: so propose: 1) Day 0-2: onboarding + share artifacts + sample script, 2) Day 3-9: run benchmarks and correctness eval, 3) Day 10-14: review results and iterate.

20:00 Liam O'Connor: ok what's required from our side for the replay?
20:05 Priya Rao: a representative prompt set (10-200 prompts) and a traffic capture or synthetic generator that matches shape. Also labeled examples for correctness metrics.
20:15 Liam O'Connor: we can export last week's traffic and a 200-example labeled set.

22:00 Priya Rao: on structured outputs, we recommend using weighted schema + strict JSON extraction and the SDK has validators that will fail if schema mismatch beyond tolerance. we'll also provide canonical function definitions for function-calling to enforce shape.
22:20 Sofia Alvarez: will we have to change our current parsing layer? we currently parse heuristically.
22:25 Priya Rao: small changes: instead of heuristic parsing you register the function signature and the model returns structured object. we also provide a post-processor to map enums to your internal ids.

25:00 Jordan Kim: cost expectations - i'll include estimated cost per 1000 requests across variants in the pilot doc. quantify batching effects.
25:10 Maya Chen: important to show cost per alert at our average size.

27:30 Priya Rao: about observability - Console will show token-level cost, per-route latency, traces for each request, and a rollout history for model pins. that should help root cause.

30:00 Liam O'Connor: can we run a quick micro-benchmark during the pilot - like 1000 short requests to measure p95 baseline?
30:06 Priya Rao: yes we'll provide the script; we can run it on your traffic replay. We'll also run with quantized 8-bit variants to compare.

33:00 Maya Chen: any blockers you've seen in similar pilots?
33:05 Priya Rao: common ones: mismatched schema expectations leading to false negatives, and underestimating burst capacity which causes throttling. we mitigate with autoscaling/burst configs and by validating function signatures early.

36:00 Jordan Kim: recap of success criteria from this call -
36:05 Sofia Alvarez: (reads) >=90% anomaly label accuracy on labeled set; p95 latency <350ms for short prompts; structured output schema validity rate >98%; cost target to be discussed after initial run but pilot should show expected $/1000 request ranges.
36:25 Jordan Kim: perfect, next steps - we will: share pilot plan and pricing (Jordan), Priya will share benchmark checklist and sample scripts, customer will provide prompt set and traffic replay. schedule infra demo for 2026-07-29.

40:00 Maya Chen: sounds good. anything else?
40:05 Liam O'Connor: one more Q - how does model fallback work if capacity constrained?
40:10 Priya Rao: smart routing will fallback to compatible model variants based on policy; you can set quality thresholds to prevent a downgrade beyond acceptable levels. we log fallbacks in console.

42:00 Jordan Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with docs and calendar invites.
42:10 Maya Chen: thanks, bye.
42:15 Sofia Alvarez: bye.

---
Meeting end: ~15:45 UTC
Recap (short): Pilot scoped for 2 weeks on hosted Redwood; objectives are latency and structured output correctness with a representative traffic replay. Action items assigned.
